item.title: Nvidia is done with Jensen Huang. The fallout in Washington is just beginning
item.description: The Republican-led Congress wants to see Jensen Huang in Washington before Democrats take control in January.

item.title: FAA grounds departing flights nationwide, citing air traffic communication system outage
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon, "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."

item.title: Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons’ firm has deep ties to the chipmaker
item.description: Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO has brought renewed scrutiny to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and his family’s financial ties to the chipmaker.

item.title: AI risks are the biggest threat to the financial system, Fed survey finds
item.description: The report comes with Wall Street on edge over high-flying AI hyperscalers, while communities are on alert for the rapid spread of data centers.

item.title: Apple, Alphabet and Uber survived major founder transitions. Nvidia will be a harder test
item.description: Like Apple, Nvidia now faces its own transition away from a founder-led company. But experts say Jensen Huang’s central role could make replacing him difficult.

item.title: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee says central bank 'has definitely got work to do' on inflation
item.description: The policymaker expressed concern about the latest inflation data, telling CNBC that the central bank likely will need to take action.

item.title: I interviewed Huang at peak ‘Jensenmania.’ Three weeks later, Nvidia is grappling with a world without him
item.description: CNBC's Arjun Kharpal, who interviewed Huang just a few weeks ago at GTC Berlin, unpacks how everything came crashing down for the popular CEO.

item.title: Alice Huang tied to Nvidia’s biggest Chinese competitor
item.description: The woman with whom Jensen Huang reportedly had a relationship also owned stakes in companies that provided computing power to Huawei, a key Nvidia competitor.

item.title: The world's super-rich are piling into alternative investments. Here's why

item.description: It comes as the U.S. continues to enforce a comprehensive economic embargo against Cuba.
